docs.title: Build your Telegram botsin a Django way.
docs.text:
Decorator routing. Edit messages and keyboards from the admin. Fully typed.

Get started Handlers

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler

@command_handler("start")
def start(ctx):
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Hello!")

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
New to the library? Read these three pages in order. Everything else can wait until you need it.

  1. Getting started: install, connect the webhook and answer /start.
  2. Handlers: reply to commands, messages and buttons.
  3. Examples: copy a working example for what you are building.

docs.title: What's inside
docs.text:
• Decorator routing

    Commands, messages, callbacks, inline queries, steps and * wildcards. Write functions or classes.

    Handlers

  • Built-in guards

    @staff_required, @superuser_required, @sponsor_required (make users join your channels first), and @before_handler for your own checks.

    Access control

  • Edit from the admin

    Messages and keyboards live in the database. Build them visually, change them without a redeploy.

    Messages & keyboards

  • Fully typed

    Every Telegram type is a Pydantic model. Autocomplete and type safety everywhere.

    Telegram client

  • Maintenance mode

    Pause the bot and show a custom message, from the admin or from code.

    Before handlers

  • Optional user model

    Let the bot create users for you, bring your own model, or use none at all.

    User model

  • Proxy and local server

    SOCKS5 proxy and local Bot API server (TDLib) support.

    Configuration

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Telegram ──webhook──▶ TelegramWebhookView
                          │
                       Dispatcher        picks a handler class by update type
                          │
                    before handlers      your checks, run on every update
                          │
                   Router.find(...)      exact → step → wildcard
                          │
                     your function or method
  1. Telegram POSTs an update to /telegram/webhook/.
  2. The Dispatcher wraps it in a handler object for its update type (command, message, callback, inline query or chosen inline result).
  3. Every @before_handler runs. If one returns True, processing stops.
  4. The Router looks for a matching route and calls it.

docs.title: Access control
docs.text:
Guards decide whether a handler runs. Put them under the route decorator.

Decorator Lets the update through when When blocked @sponsor_required the user joined every sponsor channel sends a join prompt @staff_required the database user has is_staff silent @superuser_required the database user has is_superuser silent 
from dj_telegram_bot.core.guards import sponsor_required, staff_required
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler

@command_handler("stats")
@staff_required
def stats(ctx):
    ...

Tip

When a guard blocks the update, the handler does not run and the guard returns False.

docs.title: @staff_required and @superuser_required
docs.text:
They check the flag on the database user, so they need a user model. They also block when there is no database user.

They are silent: the user gets no reply. To send a message, use @before_handler or check ctx.user_obj.is_staff inside the handler.

docs.title: @sponsor_required
docs.text: Force users to join one or more channels before the handler runs.

docs.title: 1. Add the channels
docs.text:
In the admin, open Channel sponsors and add:

Field Meaning name button label chat_id channel id; the -100 prefix is added automatically link invite or public link shown on the button is_active only active channels are checked

Warning

Add your bot as an administrator of each channel. Otherwise Telegram will not let it check membership.

docs.title: 2. Decorate the handler
docs.text:
@command_handler("start")
@sponsor_required
def start(ctx):
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Welcome!")

If the user has not joined every active channel, they get a prompt with one button per channel and a confirmation button. The handler does not run.

docs.title: 3. Handle the confirmation button
docs.text:
The confirmation button sends callback_data="sponsor_required". Register a handler for it:

from dj_telegram_bot.core.guards import SponsorGuard
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import callback_handler

@callback_handler("sponsor_required")
def sponsor_confirmed(ctx):
    if SponsorGuard(ctx).ensure_joined(use_cache=False):
        ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Thanks, you can use the bot now!")

ensure_joined() returns True if the user joined every channel. Otherwise it sends the prompt again and returns False.

docs.title: Where it applies
docs.text:
Update Checked? private chat yes group, supergroup no channel post no inline query yes button on an inline message yes

Results are cached for 60 seconds per user and channel.

docs.title: Texts
docs.text:
Texts come from Messages with these steps. English defaults are used if a message is missing.

related_step Used for Default sponsor-prompt-text the prompt message To use the bot, please join the channels below. sponsor-submit-text confirmation button label Confirm membership ✅ sponsor-join-error inline answers and callback alerts Please join the sponsor channels first, then try again.

docs.title: Advanced
Messages & keyboards
docs.text: Keep texts and keyboards in the database so you can change them from the Django admin without redeploying.

docs.title: Create a message
docs.text:
In the admin, open Messages:

  • text: the message text (HTML is the default parse mode)
  • related_step: the key you use to fetch it, for example home

Below the text there is a visual keyboard builder. A message can have one keyboard:

Field Meaning Type REPLY (reply keyboard) or INLINE resize_keyboard, one_time_keyboard reply keyboard options Buttons text, row, column and the button data below

Button data (all optional): url, callback_data, copy_text, style, request_contact, request_location, web_app, login_url, switch_inline_query_current_chat.

docs.title: Send it
docs.text:
from dj_telegram_bot.contrib.services import MessageService
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler
from dj_telegram_bot.core.keyboard import KeyboardBuilder

@command_handler("start")
def start(ctx):
    msg = MessageService.get_msg_by_step("home")
    markup = KeyboardBuilder(msg).build()
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, msg.text, reply_markup=markup)

docs.title: Options the admin cannot store
docs.text:
Some button options cannot live in the admin JSON (switch_inline_query, pay, request_poll, request_users, ...). Pass an override for one button, identified by its row and column:

from dj_telegram_bot.core.types import InlineButtonOverride

markup = KeyboardBuilder(msg).build(
    override_inline=InlineButtonOverride(row=1, column=2, switch_inline_query="cats")
)

For reply keyboards use override_reply=ReplyButtonOverride(row=..., column=..., request_poll=...).

docs.title: Messages the library reads for you
docs.text: related_step Used by block blocked users, when you call is_user_block(notify_user=True) sponsor-prompt-text sponsor prompt sponsor-submit-text sponsor confirmation button sponsor-join-error sponsor inline errors

docs.title: Before handlers
docs.text:
A before handler runs on every update, before routing. Return True to stop: no route is looked up and no handler runs.

bot_handlers/access.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import before_handler

@before_handler
def ignore_banned(ctx):
    return ctx.user_id in BANNED_IDS

OR

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import UpdateHandler, before_handler

class Guards(UpdateHandler):
    @before_handler
    def check(self):
        return self.is_user_block()
Rules:

  • They run in registration order and stop at the first one that returns True.
  • They run for every update type, even when no route would match.
  • ctx is an UpdateHandler, so every member is available whatever the update type. See Handler object.
  • The database user is loaded before they run, so ctx.user_obj costs nothing extra.
  • Returning False or None lets the update continue.
  • Registering the same function twice is ignored.

Errors stop the whole update

If a before handler raises, the update is dropped and the error is only logged. Keep them small.

user_obj can raise or be None

ctx.user_obj raises ImproperlyConfigured if your user model has no user_id and step fields, and is None for someone who never started the bot. In a check that must work everywhere, use ctx.user_id. See User model.

Built-in checks are not automatic

The library gives you two checks, is_update_mode() and is_user_block(), but does not run them for you. Register the ones you need, as shown below.

docs.title: Maintenance mode
docs.text:
ctx.is_update_mode() returns True while the bot is paused and sends the configured message.

bot_handlers/access.py
@before_handler
def maintenance(ctx):
    return ctx.is_update_mode()

Rules:

  • It only applies in private chats. Updates from groups, channels and inline mode pass through, so the bot does not spam the message there.
  • Superusers are never blocked, so you can test in production.

Turn it on from the admin (Bot update status: is_update and update_msg) or from code:

from dj_telegram_bot.contrib.services import BotStatusService

BotStatusService.set_updating(True)

Note

The status is cached for 60 seconds. set_updating() clears the cache immediately, but a change made in the admin can take up to a minute to apply.

docs.title: Blocked users
docs.text:
Set is_active = False on a user to block them, then register:

bot_handlers/access.py
@before_handler
def blocked(ctx):
    return ctx.is_user_block(notify_user=True)

is_user_block() returns True for a blocked user in every chat type, so the bot stays silent in groups and inline mode too. It only replies when you pass notify_user=True and the update comes from a private chat. The default is notify_user=False: the user is ignored without a reply.

The reply is the message with step block from the admin (Messages & keyboards), or the built-in text Access denied. Your account is currently blocked.

This check reads is_active on your user model. See User model.

Use both checks

@before_handler
def access(ctx):
    return ctx.is_update_mode() or ctx.is_user_block(notify_user=True)

docs.title: Channel membership for every update
docs.text:
@sponsor_required guards one handler. To require channel membership for every update, use the guard in a before handler.

bot_handlers/access.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.guards import SponsorGuard

@before_handler
def sponsor(ctx):
    return not SponsorGuard(ctx).ensure_joined()

Note the not

ensure_joined() returns True when the user may continue, while a before handler returns True to stop.

The same rules apply: groups and channel posts are skipped. You do not also need @sponsor_required on the handlers.

docs.title: Order matters
docs.text:
Tip

Put cheap checks first and register the ones with side effects (like sending a message) after the checks that should win. Registration order follows module import order.

docs.title: Telegram client
docs.text:
Inside a handler, ctx.bot is a typed client for the Bot API. Outside a handler (a management command, a Celery task), get the same shared client with:

from dj_telegram_bot.contrib.services import get_tm_client

bot = get_tm_client()
bot.send_message(chat_id=12345, text="Hello from a task")

docs.title: Calling methods
docs.text:
Methods mirror the Bot API in snake_case and return Pydantic models:

msg = ctx.bot.send_message(chat_id=ctx.chat_id, text="<b>Hi</b>")
print(msg.message_id)

ctx.bot.send_photo(ctx.chat_id, photo="https://example.com/cat.jpg", caption="A cat")
ctx.bot.edit_message_text(...)
ctx.bot.answer_callback_query(ctx.callback_query.id, text="Done", show_alert=True)

Every Telegram type lives in dj_telegram_bot.core.types.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text: Setting Default parse_mode "html" in most methods Link previews in send_message disabled

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Methods that upload media accept any of the following:

Type Example str a file_id or an HTTP URL bytes raw file content File object open("photo.jpg", "rb")

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Telegram errors raise TelegramAPIError, a subclass of TelegramError:

from dj_telegram_bot.core.exceptions import TelegramAPIError

try:
    ctx.bot.send_message(chat_id, "hi")
except TelegramAPIError as e:
    print(e.method, e.error_code, e.description)

Network failures and invalid responses raise the same exception with error_code == 0.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Synchronous: the client is built on requests, with a 30 second timeout (100 seconds when uploading files).
  • Cached: it is cached with lru_cache, so one client is shared per process.
  • Proxy and local server: configured with PROXY_SOCKS and TM_WEBHOOK_URL.

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
• HandlerRegistry and CommandHandler.register(...) replaced by decorators: @command_handler, @message_handler, @callback_handler, @inline_handler, @chosen_handler. Import them, and the handler classes, from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers. The routing code (core/routing.py) is internal
  • Maintenance mode and blocked-user checks no longer run automatically. Register them with @before_handler
  • is_user_block() replies only with notify_user=True
  • ctx.user is None for channel posts. Use ctx.sender
  • ChosenInlineResultHandler.query renamed to chosen_query
  • Access guards (sponsor_required, SponsorGuard, and the new staff_required and superuser_required) live in dj_telegram_bot.core.guards. sponsor_required used to be in contrib.decorators
  • Link previews are disabled by default in send_message
  • New users get their Telegram id as password (was unusable)
  • business_connection_id moved after the main parameters in the business and edit methods (edit_message_text is now chat_id, message_id, text). Use keyword arguments

See the migration guide.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• One import path: handler classes, all route decorators and @before_handler come from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers
  • UpdateHandler: one class with every member of every update type, to inherit from in class handlers. Each update type also has its own class (CommandHandler, MessageHandler, CallBackQueryHandler, InlineQueryHandler, ChosenInlineResultHandler) with only its own members.
  • @before_handler for pre-routing checks, as functions or class methods; registering a function twice is ignored. See Before handlers
  • Optional user model: any model with user_id and step works, and TelegramUserMixin.get_or_create_telegram_user() customizes creation. See User model
  • ctx.sender, ctx.has_started_bot, ctx.chosen
  • SponsorGuard.ensure_joined(), usable in a before handler for every update
  • @staff_required and @superuser_required
  • Step handlers: @message_step_handler, @callback_step_handler, and set_step()
  • Wildcard triggers with priority
  • ChosenInlineResultHandler and @chosen_handler
  • Channel post support
  • Inline queries and inline callbacks in the sponsor check. Customize the answers with @sponsor_required(on_inline=..., on_callback=...)
  • switch_inline_query_current_chat in the keyboard builder
  • Telegram Bot API updates: February to July 2026, up to 10.3

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Database users are created only in private chats; elsewhere they are only looked up. The typing chat action in groups is gone
  • Maintenance mode applies to private chats only
  • The sponsor check is skipped in groups and channels
  • AUTH_USER_MODEL is optional; the startup check for TelegramUserMixin is removed
  • Membership logic moved into SponsorGuard; enforce() stays as an alias of ensure_joined()

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Callbacks from inline messages
  • Chat and user resolution for inline and group updates
  • File name used for cover uploads
  • Shared mutable default in _add_file
Last release before the router rewrite.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Required Description BOT_TOKEN Yes Bot token from BotFather. TM_WEBHOOK_URL Yes Base URL of the Bot API: https://api.telegram.org or your local Bot API server. PROXY_SOCKS No SOCKS5 proxy as IP:PORT, used for every request to the Bot API.

Note

The client is created lazily on the first update. A missing BOT_TOKEN or TM_WEBHOOK_URL raises ValueError at that point.

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text:
You can configure a SOCKS5 proxy for your bot requests, including optional authentication credentials.

settings.py
# Format: username:password@host:port
PROXY_SOCKS = "127.0.0.1:1080"

Requests go through socks5h://PROXY_SOCKS.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
The Django cache is used for:

  • the sponsor membership check (60 seconds per user and channel)
  • the maintenance-mode status (60 seconds)

Tip

If you run several processes, use a shared cache backend (Redis, Memcached), otherwise each process keeps its own copy.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
All logs use the dj_telegram_bot logger namespace. The webhook view logs every incoming update at INFO and every unhandled exception at ERROR.

Info

The webhook view always answers Telegram with {"ok": true}, so a failing handler does not make Telegram retry the update.

settings.py
LOGGING = {
    "version": 1,
    "handlers": {"console": {"class": "logging.StreamHandler"}},
    "loggers": {"dj_telegram_bot": {"handlers": ["console"], "level": "INFO"}},
}

docs.title: Defaults of the send methods
docs.text:
• parse_mode defaults to "html" on almost all methods that accept it.
  • Link previews are disabled by default in send_message. Pass link_preview_options=LinkPreviewOptions(is_disabled=False) to enable them.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Short, copy-paste examples for common tasks. Each one links to the page that explains it in full.

Tip

Put these in a file inside bot_handlers/ (for example your_app/bot_handlers/shop.py). See Getting started.

docs.title: Handle a command
Read a command argument
docs.text:
/start ref_42 is the text start ref_42, so match with a wildcard:

bot_handlers/start.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler

@command_handler("start*")
def start(ctx):
    payload = ctx.command.removeprefix("start").strip()   # "ref_42", or "" for plain /start
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, f"Welcome! Referral: {payload or 'none'}")

More in Triggers and wildcards.

docs.title: Answer a button press
Reply to anything unmatched
Ask a question and use the answer
docs.text:
A step remembers where the user is in a conversation. This needs a user model.

bot_handlers/register.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler, message_step_handler

@command_handler("register")
def register(ctx):
    ctx.set_step("ask_name")
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "What's your name?")

@message_step_handler("ask_name")
def got_name(ctx):
    ctx.set_step("home")
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, f"Nice to meet you, {ctx.text}!")

docs.title: Keep related handlers together
Staff-only command
docs.text:
The guard goes under the route decorator. It needs a user model with is_staff. For everyone else it stays silent.

bot_handlers/admin.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.guards import staff_required
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler

@command_handler("stats")
@staff_required
def stats(ctx):
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Staff only!")

More in Access control.

docs.title: Require joining a channel
docs.text:
Add the channels in the admin first. Then guard the handler, and handle the confirmation button:

bot_handlers/start.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.guards import SponsorGuard, sponsor_required
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import callback_handler, command_handler

@command_handler("start")
@sponsor_required
def start(ctx):
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Welcome!")

@callback_handler("sponsor_required")
def sponsor_confirmed(ctx):
    if SponsorGuard(ctx).ensure_joined(use_cache=False):
        ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Thanks, you can use the bot now!")

More in the steps.

docs.title: Require joining a channel for inline queries
docs.text:
The same guard works for inline queries and for buttons on inline messages. The user gets a default answer, which you can replace:

bot_handlers/search.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.guards import sponsor_required
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import inline_handler

@inline_handler("*")
@sponsor_required
def search(ctx):
    ...  # answer the inline query

docs.title: Ignore blocked users and pause the bot
docs.text:
Maintenance mode and blocking are opt-in. Register them once:

bot_handlers/access.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import before_handler

@before_handler
def access(ctx):
    return ctx.is_update_mode() or ctx.is_user_block(notify_user=True)

Returning True stops the update. More in Before handlers.

docs.title: Send a message outside a handler
docs.text:
In a management command or a Celery task there is no ctx. Get the shared client instead:

tasks.py
from dj_telegram_bot.contrib.services import get_tm_client

bot = get_tm_client()
bot.send_message(chat_id=12345, text="Hello from a task")

More in Telegram client.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This page takes you from nothing to a bot that answers /start. It needs five short steps. Everything else is optional and can wait until you need it.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pipuv 
pip install dj_telegram_bot

uv add dj_telegram_bot

docs.title: 2. Settings
docs.text:
settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    ...
    "dj_telegram_bot.contrib",
]

BOT_TOKEN = "your-telegram-bot-token"
TM_WEBHOOK_URL = "https://api.telegram.org"  # or your local Bot API server(TDLib)

See Configuration for every setting.

docs.title: 3. URLs and migrations
docs.text:
urls.py
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    ...
    path("telegram/", include("dj_telegram_bot.contrib.urls")),
]
pythonuv 
python manage.py migrate

uv run manage.py migrate

docs.title: 4. Set the webhook
docs.text:
Run this once in your terminal. Replace <BOT_TOKEN> with your bot's token (from BotFather) and yourdomain.com with the domain your Django site runs on:

curl "https://api.telegram.org/bot<BOT_TOKEN>/setWebhook?url=https://yourdomain.com/telegram/webhook/"

Telegram answers "Webhook was set".

No public domain? Use a local Bot API server

  • Official API: the webhook url must be a public HTTPS domain.
  • Local Bot API server (TDLib): replace https://api.telegram.org with your TDLib server address (for example http://127.0.0.1:8081). The webhook url can then be your Django ip:port.

docs.title: 5. Write your first handler
docs.text:
Create a bot_handlers/ package in any Django app. Every .py file in it (except files starting with _) is imported at startup, so the handlers inside are registered automatically:

your_app/
└── bot_handlers/
    └── start.py
your_app/bot_handlers/start.py
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler

@command_handler("start")
def start(ctx):
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Hello!")

Start Django, open your bot in Telegram and send /start. It answers Hello!

docs.title: What next?
docs.text:
Pick the line that matches what you want to do:

I want to... Read reply to other commands, messages and buttons Handlers copy a working example Examples build a conversation ("what's your name?" → answer) Steps, which need a user model limit a command to staff, or require joining a channel Access control block users or pause the bot Before handlers edit texts and keyboards without redeploying Messages & keyboards

docs.title: If something doesn't work
docs.text:
Telegram never reaches your server

Ask Telegram what it sees (use your local server's address instead if you run one):

curl "https://api.telegram.org/bot<BOT_TOKEN>/getWebhookInfo"

last_error_message says why delivery failed, and pending_update_count shows updates that are waiting.

The bot never answers

Check your logs. If a module in bot_handlers/ raises on import, the error is logged and the module is skipped.

/start works but /start something doesn't

The trigger must match the whole text after the slash. Use "start*". See command arguments.

Nothing happens and there is no error

An update that matches no handler is silently ignored.

docs.title: Handlers outside bot_handlers/
Handler object
docs.text: This page is a reference. You do not need to read it top to bottom: come here when you want to know what ctx (in a function handler) or self (in a class handler) can do.

docs.title: On every handler
docs.text:
Member Description bot the Telegram client update the raw Update text message text or caption ("" if none) message the message (for a callback, the message the button belongs to) callback_query, inline_query, chosen the matching part of the update, or None query the inline query text ("" if none) inline_message_id set for buttons on inline messages chat, chat_id where to answer (chat_id is 0 if there is no chat) user, user_id the Telegram user who sent the update (None and 0 for channel posts) sender the user, or for channel posts the sender chat or the channel is_private(), is_group(), is_inline_callback() where the update came from has_joined_channel(chat_id, user_id) membership check is_update_mode(), is_user_block() the built-in checks

Groups, channels and inline updates

For channel posts there is no user: use sender. For buttons on inline messages chat is the user themselves, because the real chat is unknown. Database users are created only in private chats; see User model.

is_private()

is_private() is True for private chats. For inline queries it follows the query's chat_type, and for buttons on inline messages it is always False, because the real location is unknown.

docs.title: The database user
docs.text:
See User model for how to set it up.

Member Description user_obj your database user, or None has_started_bot True if a database user exists user_step the current step, or "" set_step(step) save a new step on the database user

docs.title: Per update type
docs.text:
These also exist on UpdateHandler.

Member Class Description command CommandHandler text without the leading / ("" if not a command) callback_data CallBackQueryHandler the button's callback_data result_id ChosenInlineResultHandler the chosen result's id chosen_query ChosenInlineResultHandler the query typed before the result was chosen

docs.title: Handlers
docs.text:
A handler is a function (or a method) that runs when an update matches a trigger. You write it, decorate it with the trigger, and the library does the routing.

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler

@command_handler("start")
def start(ctx):
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Hello!")

ctx is the handler object: it gives you the bot, the chat, the text, the user and more. The full list is in Handler object.

docs.title: Pick a decorator
docs.text:
Most bots use @command_handler, @message_handler and @callback_handler. The others cover steps, inline mode and channel posts.

Decorator Runs for Trigger is matched against @command_handler messages starting with / the text without the leading /, including arguments @message_handler every other message, and channel posts the text (or caption) @message_step_handler same as above the user's current step @callback_handler inline button presses callback_data @callback_step_handler inline button presses the user's current step @inline_handler inline queries the query text @chosen_handler a chosen inline result the result_id Imports 
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import (
    command_handler,
    message_handler,
    callback_handler,
    inline_handler,
    chosen_handler,
    message_step_handler,
    callback_step_handler,
)

docs.title: Function or class?
docs.text:
Tip

Start with functions. Reach for a class when you want to keep related handlers together.

docs.title: Function handlers
docs.text:
The function receives the handler object, conventionally named ctx. Type-hint it to get autocomplete:

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import CommandHandler, command_handler

@command_handler("start")
def start(ctx: CommandHandler):
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Hello!")

The class of ctx depends on the decorator:

Decorator ctx is a @command_handler CommandHandler @message_handler, @message_step_handler MessageHandler @callback_handler, @callback_step_handler CallBackQueryHandler @inline_handler InlineQueryHandler @chosen_handler ChosenInlineResultHandler

One function can serve several triggers by stacking decorators:

@command_handler("help")
@message_handler("Help")
def help_(ctx):
    ...

docs.title: Class handlers
docs.text:
Group related handlers in a class. Inherit from UpdateHandler and decorate methods:

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import UpdateHandler, command_handler, callback_handler

class Shop(UpdateHandler):
    @command_handler("shop")
    def open_shop(self):
        self.bot.send_message(self.chat_id, "Welcome to the shop")

    @callback_handler("buy_*")
    def buy(self):
        item = self.callback_data.removeprefix("buy_")
        self.bot.answer_callback_query(self.callback_query.id, text=f"Added {item}")

UpdateHandler has every member of every update type, so your editor shows self.bot, self.chat_id, self.callback_data and the rest in any method.

Note

Members that belong to another update type are empty ("" or None): self.callback_data is "" inside a @command_handler method.

Note

The library creates your class as Shop(update, bot) when a route matches. If you override __init__, keep that signature and call super().__init__(update, bot).

If a class only handles one update type, you can inherit from that class instead (CallBackQueryHandler, CommandHandler, ...). BaseHandler has only the members common to every update.

docs.title: Triggers and wildcards
docs.text:
A trigger is an exact string, or a string with *:

Trigger Matches "start" exactly start "buy_*" anything starting with buy_ "*_done" anything ending with _done "*promo*" anything containing promo "*" everything

* is only allowed at the start, the end, or both. "a*b" raises ValueError when the module loads.

Command arguments

ctx.command is the whole text after the slash. /start gives "start", but /start ref_42 gives "start ref_42", and /start@MyBot gives "start@MyBot". Use "start*" to accept arguments:

@command_handler("start*")
def start(ctx):
    payload = ctx.command.removeprefix("start").strip()   # "ref_42"

docs.title: Lookup order
docs.text:
For every update the router tries, in this order, and uses the first match:

  1. exact trigger
  2. the user's step (message and callback handlers only)
  3. wildcards, highest priority first, then the longest literal part
@message_handler("*", priority=-10)      # fallback, tried last
def fallback(ctx): ...

@message_handler("buy_*")
def buy(ctx): ...

@message_handler("buy_premium_*")        # longer literal, wins over "buy_*"
def buy_premium(ctx): ...

Warning

Registering the same trigger twice with different functions logs a warning (Pattern 'x' in message overridden) and the last one wins.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
A step is a short string stored on the user (user.step, default "home"). It lets you build conversations: ask something, set a step, handle the next message.

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler, message_step_handler

@command_handler("register")
def register(ctx):
    ctx.set_step("ask_name")
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "What's your name?")

@message_step_handler("ask_name")
def got_name(ctx):
    ctx.set_step("home")
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, f"Nice to meet you, {ctx.text}!")

Warning

Step handlers need a database user with user_id and step fields. Without one, user_step is an empty string and they never match.

  • An exact trigger always wins over a step, so a user in ask_name who taps a button with an exact handler still reaches that handler.
  • Step handlers also fire for non-text messages (photo, contact, location). ctx.text is empty in that case.
  • callback_step_handler does the same for inline button presses.

docs.title: Unmatched updates
docs.text:
Info

If nothing matches, the update is silently ignored. Add a @message_handler("*", priority=-10) if you want a fallback reply.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Examples: working examples you can copy.
  • Handler object: everything ctx / self gives you.

docs.title: Migration guide: 0.1.x → 0.2
docs.text:
The routing layer was rewritten. Most bots need only a few mechanical changes.

Info

The "before" examples come from the 0.1.4 README. If you used other 0.1.x APIs, check them against the Handlers page.

The short version

Replace @Class.register(...) with a decorator, import routing from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers, and register @before_handler checks if you used maintenance mode or blocked users.

docs.title: 1. Handlers: register → decorators
docs.text:
HandlerRegistry was replaced by a Router, and CommandHandler.register(...) no longer exists. Use decorators directly on your handler methods.

Before (0.1.x)After (0.2) 
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import CommandHandler

class StartHandler(CommandHandler):
    @CommandHandler.register("start")
    def start(self):
        self.bot.send_message(chat_id=self.chat_id, text="Hello!")

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import CommandHandler, command_handler

class StartHandler(CommandHandler):
    @command_handler("start")
    def start(self):
        self.bot.send_message(chat_id=self.chat_id, text="Hello!")
Update Decorator command @command_handler message @message_handler, @message_step_handler callback @callback_handler, @callback_step_handler inline query @inline_handler chosen inline result @chosen_handler

docs.title: 2. Imports
docs.text:
Handler classes, every route decorator and before_handler are imported from one module, dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers:

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import (
    UpdateHandler,
    before_handler,
    command_handler,
    message_handler,
    callback_handler,
)

The routing code lives in core/routing.py, but that module is internal. Don't import from it.

sponsor_required moved from contrib.decorators to core.guards:

- from dj_telegram_bot.contrib.decorators import sponsor_required
+ from dj_telegram_bot.core.guards import sponsor_required

docs.title: 3. Maintenance mode and user blocking are optional
docs.text:
In 0.1.x these checks ran automatically. Now you register them as before handlers. To keep the old behavior, including the reply to blocked users:

from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import before_handler

@before_handler
def check_user_and_bot_status(ctx):
    return ctx.is_update_mode() or ctx.is_user_block(notify_user=True)

Without these, blocked users and maintenance mode have no effect.

docs.title: 4. Sponsor confirmation button
docs.text: Handle the sponsor_required callback, see Access control.

docs.title: Behavior changes
docs.text: Change Action Maintenance mode applies to private chats only none, unless you relied on it in groups is_user_block() stays silent unless you pass notify_user=True pass it to keep the reply Blocked users are ignored in every chat type, not just private none Database users are created only in private chats. In groups and inline mode they are only looked up, and there is no typing chat action none; ctx.user_obj can now be None, so check ctx.has_started_bot ctx.user is None for channel posts (it used to be the channel) use ctx.sender ChosenInlineResultHandler.query is now chosen_query. query is the inline query text rename the attribute SponsorGuard.enforce() is now ensure_joined(); enforce still works none The sponsor check is skipped in groups and for channel posts none, unless you relied on it in groups New users get their Telegram id as password. In 0.1.x it was unusable set a real password before is_staff, or override creation Link previews are disabled by default in send_message pass link_preview_options=LinkPreviewOptions(is_disabled=False) to restore AUTH_USER_MODEL is optional; the startup check for TelegramUserMixin is gone none In methods that take business_connection_id, it is no longer the first parameter. edit_message_text now takes chat_id, message_id, text in that order pass arguments by keyword; a positional call can silently send the wrong value Telegram types follow the newer Bot API, so some fields changed or were added re-run your type checker

docs.title: New features worth adopting
docs.text:
• UpdateHandler as the one class to inherit from, and one import path for routing: dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers
  • @before_handler for your own pre-routing checks, including a channel membership check for every update
  • Your own user model, and get_or_create_telegram_user() to customize creation
  • ctx.has_started_bot and ctx.sender
  • @staff_required and @superuser_required
  • Step handlers and ctx.set_step()
  • Channel posts and chosen inline results
  • Wildcard priority

docs.title: User model
docs.text: dj_telegram_bot can keep a database row for every Telegram user. It is used for steps, blocking users, and staff checks. A user model is optional.

docs.title: Three ways to set it up
docs.text:
Your AUTH_USER_MODEL Users are user_obj, steps, blocking inherits TelegramUserMixin created for you work has real user_id and step fields, no mixin only looked up, never created work for users you created yourself neither (for example Django's default User) not used user_obj raises ImproperlyConfigured; steps never match; blocking does nothing

Note

"Real" means a normal field, not a relation. A ForeignKey named user creates a user_id attribute, but it does not count.

docs.title: With TelegramUserMixin
docs.text:
your_app/models.py
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser
from dj_telegram_bot.contrib.mixins import TelegramUserMixin

class User(AbstractUser, TelegramUserMixin):
    pass
settings.py
AUTH_USER_MODEL = "your_app.User"

The mixin adds two fields, so run makemigrations and migrate:

Field Type user_id BigIntegerField, unique: the Telegram user id step CharField(max_length=30), default "home"

docs.title: When users are created
docs.text:
Users are created only in private chats: the first time someone writes to the bot. Everywhere else (groups, channels, inline messages) the bot only looks the user up, so ctx.user_obj is None for someone who never started the bot.

Use ctx.has_started_bot to ask whether a database user exists.

docs.title: What gets filled in
docs.text:
get_or_create_telegram_user() fills only the fields your model has:

Field Value username the Telegram username, or the user id first_name the Telegram first name last_name the Telegram last name, or "" password the Telegram user id, hashed

docs.title: With your own model
docs.text:
Skip the mixin and add the two fields yourself:

your_app/models.py
user_id = models.BigIntegerField(unique=True)
step = models.CharField(max_length=30, default="home")

The bot never creates these users. Create them yourself, for example in /start:

bot_handlers/start.py
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from dj_telegram_bot.core.handlers import command_handler

User = get_user_model()

@command_handler("start")
def start(ctx):
    User.objects.get_or_create(
        user_id=ctx.user_id,
        defaults={"username": str(ctx.user_id)},
    )
    ctx.bot.send_message(ctx.chat_id, "Welcome!")

Info

Two built-in checks read standard fields: is_user_block() reads is_active, and is_update_mode() reads is_superuser. Models based on AbstractUser have both.

docs.title: Using the user
Customizing creation
docs.text:
Override get_or_create_telegram_user() on your model. It receives the Telegram User and must return a model instance.

Add your own fieldsUnusable password your_app/models.py
class User(AbstractUser, TelegramUserMixin):
    language = models.CharField(max_length=5, default="en")

    @classmethod
    def get_or_create_telegram_user(cls, tg_user):
        user, _ = cls.objects.get_or_create(
            user_id=tg_user.id,
            defaults={
                "username": tg_user.username or str(tg_user.id),
                "first_name": tg_user.first_name,
                "language": tg_user.language_code or "en",
            },
        )
        return user
your_app/models.py
    @classmethod
    def get_or_create_telegram_user(cls, tg_user):
        user, created = cls.objects.get_or_create(
            user_id=tg_user.id,
            defaults={"username": tg_user.username or str(tg_user.id)},
        )
        if created:
            user.set_unusable_password()
            user.save(update_fields=["password"])

        return user

Warning

If your model has a required field the default cannot fill (for example an email without a default), creation fails with an IntegrityError. Override the method as above.
